28. Although the following terms may be used by gay people themselves, they should not be
used by judges:
• Gays/a gay.
• Homosexuals/a homosexual.

Sexual orientation
Equal Treatment Bench Book – July 2024 (February 2026 update) 183
• Dyke.
• Queer.

29. The term “queer” is widely used amongst certain demographics. Nevertheless, it is still
considered derogatory by many people in the LGB communities, and it is therefore to be
avoided by judges.
The Equality Act 2010
The EqA 2010 prohibits discrimination in relation to sexual orientation. There have been a number
of cases where gay discrimination for religious reasons in the public sphere has been held
unlawful. See the Equality Act 2010 appendix for an overview of the EqA 2010 and for more detail
of the application of the EqA 2010 to sexual orientation.
